A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same YOTO research work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, support reliable comparison; retained material can be matched across renumbering.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A report original classification experiments on VISp and COVID-PBMC, including baseline comparisons and a selection-module ablation.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds classifier controls, multi-task ablations, gene-selection stability analyses and biological enrichment results.

M1.justification: The learned gene scores, differentiable ranking, straight-through binary selection, progressive sparsification, shared encoder and task-specific losses remain unchanged. The added Random Forest evaluation and architecture controls test the existing method; the implementation appendix does not establish a revised core algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate VISp and COVID-PBMC with the same supervised targets and gene-panel size ranges. The added classifier, stability and marker/GO analyses examine the existing data and selected panels, without introducing a new prediction population, domain or input scenario.

E2.justification: The main comparisons add YOTO (FS only), which predicts with a Random Forest trained on YOTO-selected genes, while retaining all six original baselines. Appendix A.2.1 additionally evaluates multi-task Random Forest variants of Seurat and Seurat v3.

E3.justification: v2 substantially extends the evaluation design with isolated panel evaluation, matched-architecture single-task versus multi-task controls, a larger-capacity condition, and multi-task Random Forest comparisons. It also introduces gene-overlap, GO-rank concordance and cross-size containment protocols. The original 80-20 split and 1000-epoch budget remain; cell-level splitting and macro-F1 are newly clarified, not demonstrated protocol changes.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained selection-module ablation, v2 tests panel quality separately from classifier choice and multi-task learning separately from model capacity. Sections 4.4.6-4.4.7 add seed stability, known-marker enrichment, functional concordance and panel nestedness analyses; Appendix A.2.1 examines single-task versus multi-task baseline classifiers.

E5.justification: Existing benchmark reporting retains means and standard deviations across seeds 0, 1 and 2. Section 4.4.6 newly introduces Fisher's exact test, with an odds ratio and p-value for marker enrichment. This adds inferential reporting without establishing an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results for FS-only prediction, controlled multi-task comparisons, baseline classifier variants and biological stability. Most matched benchmark entries remain unchanged, but VISp F1 at 32 genes changes from 84.8 ± 0.0 in v1 Table 5 to 82.7 ± 2.7 in v2 Table 6. New Tables 2-3 show FS-only YOTO outperforming integrated YOTO on VISp, but not COVID-PBMC, contrary to the added prose.

T1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds an explicit mathematical specification of the exponential subset-size annealing schedule in Equations 8-9, where v1 described progressive annealing qualitatively. This is a limited formalization: the core ranking, masking and loss equations remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retreat from prominent claims about benefiting from partially labeled datasets, and the conclusion explicitly leaves experimental validation of that benefit to future work. Resource-efficiency wording is also softened. The central contributions of discrete, end-to-end selection and joint multi-task prediction remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive qualifications about generalization to unseen cells rather than unseen patients, patient-specific confounding, sparse-panel task tradeoffs and the need for shared biological structure. It acknowledges that multi-task learning is not always optimal and partial-label benefits remain untested. New stability discussions interpret variable gene identities through functional redundancy and stabilization of a core panel.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.3 documents software packages, SMOTE, Random Forest settings, optimizers, architectures, batch sizes, learning rates, temperature schedules and sparsification schedules, including Tables 11-15. v2 also clarifies split granularity and F1 averaging and supplies a code-access link. These are substantial disclosures, not evidence that previously reported experiments were changed or rerun.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting multi-task learning, SMOTE and biological marker validation, including Kurin, Liu, He, Chawla and Tasic. It qualifies PERSIST's end-to-end status in Table 1 and clarifies the relationship to Grover et al.'s ranking operator. The main related-work narrative and nearest comparison remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section order and much existing prose are retained, with targeted rewrites, expanded explanations and additional experimental and implementation subsections. Author/publication information expands and acknowledgments disappear. v2 also introduces a duplicated abstract sentence and an unfinished '[...]' phrase in Section 4.4.6.

P2.justification: Figure 1 adds a feedback arrow, Figure 2 adds the FS-only series, and new Figures 4-5 visualize overlap, GO concordance and nestedness. Comparative tables gain pipeline columns, FS-only rows and revised highlighting; new ablation and implementation tables substantially expand the displays. The original class-distribution figure is retained as Figure 6.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially addresses v1's missing implementation specifications and limited evidence isolating gene-panel quality and stability through Appendix A.3, classifier controls and new robustness analyses. Explicit limits on patient generalization and partial-label claims also improve scientific qualification. These gains outweigh localized reporting and editing problems, including the duplicated abstract text and the COVID-PBMC FS-only claim contradicted by Table 2.
